Lecture notes: fluid balance

Water moves between compartments by osmosis. Sodium is the main extracellular cation and potassium the main intracellular one. Thirst and antidiuretic hormone keep plasma osmolality within a narrow range, and the kidney adjusts what it excretes to what is taken in.

In children the proportion of body water is higher, so losses from vomiting or diarrhoea deplete them faster. Replacement is planned as deficit, maintenance and ongoing losses.
